subject: bauhausBird
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: songbird on a branch.
Style: Bauhaus primary-colour geometry.
reasoning:
I'm sketching a compact Bauhaus-style songbird on a branch: a red circular body, blue triangular wing, yellow tail and beak, with simple black line details and white accents for the eye, perched on a dark wood branch.

I'm working out the skeleton structure next—placing the root hip joint at the body center, with a chain rising through chest, neck, and head joints, keeping the rig lightweight at roughly 300 lines.

For the body geometry, I'm sculpting the torso with a scaled sphere bound to the chest bone, using a flat red paint with a countershaded cream belly to give it that Bauhaus-style contrast.

Now I'm planning the head as a yellow sphere with a black triangular-prism beak made from narrow cones pointing forward along the neck direction, plus a smaller lower jaw cone, and eyes placed via decal textures on the head.

Still building geometry... now adding a black extruded triangle crest on the head, and setting up wing shoulder joints with angled triangular outlines for the blue wings.

Setting up the wing joint with a slight outward angle for a more natural splayed pose, computing the correct thickness axis, then layering a smaller yellow triangle with offset to suggest a stripe detail.

Now I'm building the tail as a chain of three bone points tapering back from the hips, using a frustum/sweep shape with a box cross-section that narrows toward the tip for a tapered blue tail.

I'm color-banding the tail blue near the base, yellow in the middle, and black at the tip, then moving on to leg geometry: defining hip-to-foot limb chains with knee bends pointing backward to mimic a bird's leg structure.

Now I'm setting up the toe chains, placing three toes forward and one back at the ankle, positioning the foot on top of the branch mesh based on its radius and centerline.

Adding toe rods...

I'm plotting the branch curve with four control points rising slightly toward the center, keeping the radius low enough that the bird's feet rest right at the branch surface, adjusting the lowest point so it just grazes the floor within tolerance.

Still working out leg lengths and foot placement so the hip-to-toe distance stays within limb reach, then adding a couple of small twig spikes branching off the main branch.

For decoration I'm thinking Bauhaus-style accents—tiny flat discs for leaves in red/blue/yellow using thin cylinder geometry, plus maybe cheek discs on the head for a playful touch, while keeping the overall texture count low.

For the wing, instead of a texture I'm painting procedural color bands along one axis to get blue/black/red/blue stripes, which gives a geometric Bauhaus look without needing an actual image texture. Then I'm positioning the beak pieces—upper beak attached to the head bone, lower beak at a jaw joint placed slightly below and in front, aimed forward for a natural open-mouth pose.

I'm settling on a color scheme: red body, yellow head, blue wing, black beak, striped tail, and white/black eyes, then shaping the head as a small flattened sphere positioned above the body with a connecting neck piece.

Positioning the neck and body spheres so they overlap smoothly, placing the yellow head sphere at the top, then working out where the wing attaches on the body's side given the body's narrowing width near the shoulder.

Now I'm sketching a black triangular crest attached at the top of the head, angled backward, and setting up the eye placement using a direction vector from the head center scaled by the head radius to position small circular eye discs.

I'm defining the eye and cheek disc colors and sizes, with left/right mirroring via the sign variable, and building the eye texture with white sclera, black pupil, and a highlight dot rendered via SVG circles mapped onto the circle geometry.

Now I'm assigning rig roles to each joint—spine, neck, head, jaw, wing, tail, leg—so the skeleton chains can be identified functionally, and setting up the wing joint attached to the chest with a direction angled outward and backward.

Writing wing tip and leg chain code...

Toes sink slightly below the branch surface for grounding. For the tail, I'm chaining three joints with decreasing height and width for a natural taper, built from boxes. I'll skip the glow effect, paint the branch with a darker grain texture, and finalize the export using the agentic-3js-builder imports, computing offsets directly rather than relying on Vector3 helpers.
